newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-INTER SAYS HAS VERBAL AGREEMENT WITH RONALDO.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-INTER SAYS HAS VERBAL AGREEMENT WITH RONALDO.

text.p: Internazionale Milan president Massimo Moratti said on Thursday he had Ronaldo's word that the Brazilian striker would join the Italian club, but said a formal signing would have to wait.
"With Ronaldo and those who represent him there is the substantial agreement, but not a formal one," Moratti told reporters on returning to Milan from Rome.
"For the signature we will have to wait until the end of June or early July, when the player no longer has commitments with the Brazilian national team."
Moratti said he was convinced the long-running saga of Ronaldo's future was ending, despite the fact the current world player of the year had not signed anything.
"Both he and his agents have given me assurances. For the first time in football I think that it is right to trust in an agreement that has not yet been completed," said Moratti.
Moratti ruled out a trip to France to ensure Ronaldo's signature, saying the Barcelona player had enough on his mind with the four-nation Tournoi de France.
"Obviously everything must be wrapped up in his presence, but there are no more problems," Moratti said.
The deal would make the Brazilian the world's most costly soccer star.
The Ansa news agency said Ronaldo was set to reap $3 million net a year plus a one-off $14 million from the deal. There would also be a payment of 45 billion lire ($27 million) to Barcelona.
Ronaldo was earlier quoted as saying he hoped to make an announcement on Thursday evening and confirmed he would be leaving Barcelona.

Inter, who splashed out on a host of foreign stars last year including England midfielder Paul Ince and France's Youri Djorkaeff, finished third in the league last season and will play in the UEFA Cup competition in 1997-98.
Barcelona are in the European Cup Champions' League.
